system.summary: Truppenschlüssel: single-stage two-square substitution of consecutive plaintext pairs with two 5x5 squares (no J), the in-line case taking right neighbours (Ostwald and Weierud).
system.sibling_key: None known for 4 July; the keys changed daily. The net ib9 key of 30 June 1941 (broken by George Lasry in 2022) was used only as a solver control.
system.notes: TS conventions (Ostwald and Weierud): J written II, CH as Q, X as separator. All 9 repeats of 6 or more letters start at equal parity, as a fixed pair substitution requires (ts_check.py). Nr. 96 and 97 are nearly the same text; Nr. 90 and 91 share a 13-letter ending.

prior_solution.where: CryptoCellar, 1941 Message List, status 20 Oct 2026 (https://cryptocellar.org/bgac/1941-msg-list.html): 'Nr. 88 to Nr. 97 broken by Norbert Paefgen on 21.09.2026 and Ben Davies (AI) on 25.09.2026'. The break is announced there; the plaintexts and keys are not published. The older 'unbroken' TS page (27 Jul 2026), the catalogue's source, still lists the messages.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; the rule control, solver runs, facsimile check and prior-art check were done by AI language-model agents. No hand correction recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the CryptoCellar TS page, the 1941 Message List, the BGAC index and the Ostwald and Weierud author copy (mcts.pdf); copied the eight 4 July messages into messages.txt.

Read the facsimiles of Nr. 88, 94 and 95 and compared them with the transcription: the groups match in order; Nr. 88 has 38 cells against 40 declared; Nr. 94 group 23 is blank. The Nr. 95 link on the TS page is broken.
TS rule control on the paper's examples: Fig. 2 key 4/4; the 17 Sep 1941 pairs with the Fig. 6 squares agree on 24/28 and 117/126 letters, every differing pair a one-letter garble.
All 9 repeats of 6 or more letters in the 4 July messages start at equal parity, consistent with a fixed pair substitution; Nr. 96 and 97 belong together.

Solver control on the broken net ib9 set of 30 June 1941 (Nr. 62-70, about 400 letters): broken in 1 of 16 restarts (a second solver: 2 of 16), score -4.71 per 4-gram (second solver -4.72); 2,000 random keys at most -7.53, the right key with 4 random swaps about -6.5. The 14 July 1941 control (194 letters) was not broken.

Joint annealing of both squares on all 8 messages (694 cells), on the 6 pz6-marked messages, with pairs swapped, and with an X-separator language model: no German; best -6.01 to -6.16 per 4-gram. A second solver gave -6.15. Net nfw (3 Jul, Nr. 84-86) was not broken either.
Crib HARTIIENSTEIN on the 13-letter end repeat of Nr. 90/91: the crib fits a TS key (23 of 26 letters) but the rest stays gibberish.

Found the September 2026 breaks on the 1941 Message List (https://cryptocellar.org/bgac/1941-msg-list.html): Nr. 88-97 broken by Norbert Paefgen (21.09.2026) and Ben Davies (AI) (25.09.2026). Plaintexts and keys not published. Re-fetched the pages the same evening; the copies were identical.

outcome.method_basis: Our ciphertext-only annealing gave no German on the 4 July messages, though it broke a 400-letter control set; the messages were broken in September 2026 by Norbert Paefgen and Ben Davies (AI), whose plaintexts and keys are not published.
outcome.fraction_read_source: No reading file: no cipher letter was given a value here.
